claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase, dendritic BCC material.
TiVNbTa has a room-temperature yield strength of about 330 MPa and approximately 40% strain.
At 1273 K, TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa and compressive strength of about 423 MPa.
The reported TiVNbTa baseline sustains around 40% strain at 1273 K.
A controlled carbon addition and heat treatment can form TiC precipitates in a refractory HEA matrix.
The intervention will produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale TiC precipitates in TiVNbTa.
The TiC precipitates will be coherent with the TiVNbTa matrix.
Fine TiC precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby provide second-phase strengthening.
TiC precipitation will contribute to grain refinement in TiVNbTa.
TiC precipitation will improve high-temperature yield-strength retention in TiVNbTa.
The modified TiVNbTa will approach or surpass 400 MPa yield strength at approximately 1273 K.
The strengthening intervention will preserve acceptable ductility.
Coherent TiC interfaces will preserve efficient heat transfer between adjacent W and CuCrZr layers.
The carbon addition will not compromise high-temperature thermal conductivity at the W-to-CuCrZr interfaces.
Excess carbon or inappropriate processing could cause precipitate coarsening, embrittlement, or degraded interfacial thermal properties.
Performance is to be assessed near 1273 K under compressive loading at strains up to about 40%.
The strength improvement and retained ductility depend sensitively on carbon content and heat-treatment parameters.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state assigns approximately 330 MPa yield strength and 40% strain to room temperature, whereas the baseline assigns approximately 330 MPa yield strength and around 40% strain to 1273 K, leaving the temperature attribution internally inconsistent.
